@@ -0,0 +1,28 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+set -euo pipefail
+
+package_spec=$(node -p 'const {name, version} = require("./package.json"); name + "@" + version')
+scratch=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'rm -rf -- "$scratch"' EXIT
+cd "$scratch"
+touch npmrc
+unset NODE_AUTH_TOKEN NPM_TOKEN
+
+# Use a clean cache and config so a consumer can obtain the exact tarball.
+# npm retries transient HTTP errors. Retry a new version's 404 briefly while
+# the public registry propagates it.
+for attempt in 1 2 3; do
+  if npm pack "$package_spec" --ignore-scripts --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org \
+    --userconfig=/dev/null --globalconfig="$scratch/npmrc" --cache="$scratch/cache" \
+    --prefer-online --fetch-timeout=15000 --fetch-retries=1 >pack.log 2>&1; then
+    cat pack.log
+    printf 'Downloaded %s anonymously from npm.\n' "$package_spec"
+    exit 0
+  fi
+  if [[ "$attempt" == 3 ]] || ! grep -q 'code E404' pack.log; then
+    cat pack.log >&2
+    printf 'Could not download %s anonymously from npm. Check public visibility and retry verification.\n' "$package_spec" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  sleep "$((attempt * 5))"
+done

Reproduction

Run `/fix --ci-cd` on a repository with a required root-layout check that disallows arbitrary root files, such as link-foundation/link-cli. The initial draft commit can contain only the generated root `.gitkeep`.

In the observed [draft](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/pull/208), [commit 26852bd](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/commit/26852bd276b6cdeef98316fae6d2526e2de80483) created the placeholder. The [required JavaScript stage](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/46067171135) failed with `.gitkeep should live under the package-specific project tree or case-study evidence`. The shared stage gate then prevented Rust and C# checks from running. link-foundation/link-cli#207 collects the logs. Earlier placeholder cleanup work in #1528 and #2215 addresses expensive path-filtered jobs and preventing a placeholder from leaking into a final merge. Required checks can still fail as soon as the draft opens.

A local reproduction from a clean checkout of that repo is to add a root `.gitkeep`, stage it, and run `node --test js/test/repositoryLayout.test.mjs` (or run the JavaScript stage's `npm run test:js` command inside `js/`).

### Workaround and proposed change

Remove the generated file as part of the first real patch. Keep the repository's required checks and root allowlist in place.

Teach the draft creation path to try a payload-free Git commit where the host accepts an empty comparison, or allow a repository-configured placeholder path before falling back to a root file. If GitHub rejects a compare without a content diff, use the configured path instead. Keep the existing cleanup and placeholder-only detection for the fallback. Add a regression that prepares a solver draft against a repository with an unconditional layout guard and verifies that a supported placeholder strategy leaves the required check green.

+{"body":"The reported C# failure was a macOS hosted-runner acquisition outage: the job never executed a step. This PR also fixes independent checks that could report success while dropping link errors, accepting incomplete CodeQL extraction, ignoring failed prerequisites, or skipping committed logs during secrets scanning.

Fixes #165

- Use an available C# macOS runner and add bounded recovery only for confirmed runner-acquisition failures. Ordinary test failures remain failures.
- Validate every workflow prerequisite, SARIF invocation/diagnostic, maintained NuGet graph and Cargo warning. Preserve reports on failure and add default-off verbose diagnostics.
- Detect lockfile/helper-only changes, full merges on main and source moves into excluded folders; fail on missing Git evidence or output writes while preserving per-commit PR detection.
- Fix adjacent-link parsing, bound transient retries, preserve archive fallback, and fail on missing or malformed evidence.
- Repair JavaScript/C# CodeQL extraction and stale overlay diagnostics; keep the full client conformance coverage and all native OS matrices.
- Add complete maintained JavaScript/Python formatting, lint/type checks and local hooks; audit every Cargo/npm/NuGet/Python dependency set. Refresh outdated dependencies and prepare Rust/C# patch releases through existing changesets.
- Authenticate before main release builds, retain PR advisory behavior, cancel superseded read-only checks, and serialize release/deployment writers.

The [audit and requirements matrix](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/blob/issue-165-a5206aa5b4c0/dev/log/issues/165/pulls/166/analysis/AUDIT.md) contains root causes, alternatives and executed plans for every requirement and all seventeen best-practice principles. The [evidence index](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/blob/issue-165-a5206aa5b4c0/dev/log/issues/165/pulls/166/README.md) links 93 collected runs, full available logs/annotations, the event timeline, immutable snapshots of four templates, and a comparison of all 1,063 tree entries.

Reproduction and validation:

- `node experiments/issue-165/reproduce-template-gaps.mjs` runs the original template helpers and repaired implementations on identical inputs: two adjacent broken links previously became one, and extraction-error SARIF previously passed.
- `node experiments/issue-165/reproduce-ignored-secret.mjs` verifies that both ignored plain logs and compressed logs are scanned and reject a synthetic secret.
- 282 local helper/repository tests plus five Rust detector tests pass; all 81 maintained JavaScript and 16 Python files pass formatting/lint, and both runtime CI helpers pass strict mypy.
- `python experiments/issue-165/reproduce-change-detection.py` proves the original/fixed Rust lock/helper flags and failed Git/output exit statuses with a focused one-job build.
- All ten workflows passed on `fd17aa4`, `8f24ffd` and `5db14dd`, including the additional change-detection fixes. The final follow-up runs full CodeQL queries directly to avoid the compare API’s 300-file limit; validation of `917b6ef` passes in all ten workflows below. Full native Rust/.NET/Wasm builds, fresh-merge checks, security scans and Node/Bun/Deno backend conformance run in CI.

Shared defects were reported with reproductions, workarounds and code suggestions: [Rust template #228](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/228), [C# template #98](https://github.com/link-foundation/csharp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/98), [JS template #286](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/286), [Python template #137](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/137), [CodeQL #23036](https://github.com/github/codeql/issues/23036), [CodeQL #23037](https://github.com/github/codeql/issues/23037), [CodeQL Action #4307](https://github.com/github/codeql-action/issues/4307), and [CodeQL Action #4308](https://github.com/github/codeql-action/issues/4308).

The recovery trigger becomes active after the workflow reaches main; its classification and retry bounds are tested offline before merge. Registry probes do not publish packages, and NuGet authentication is explicitly distinguished from package push authorization, which the real publication must enforce. The original unexplained Rust upload failure remains documented with the available evidence and opt-in diagnostics; subsequent fresh Rust analyses pass.

Known external diagnostics are fully inventoried in the [final verification record](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/blob/issue-165-a5206aa5b4c0/dev/log/issues/165/pulls/166/analysis/final-verification.md). On final head `917b6ef`, GitHub’s [CodeQL comparison summary](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/runs/127647402772) is neutral only because of the obsolete, pre-existing C# `autobuild` baseline configuration; all five current categories are present and pass. The earlier stale pending-category summary is reported upstream, with the final observation added to that report. Dependency Review’s 23 low OpenSSF project-practice scores remain visible, while vulnerability audits pass. Historical security configurations and warning thresholds are preserved.

+{"body":"## Summary

Fixes #172

This PR audits every warning, error, false positive and false negative in the `main` runs at `199a07b` listed in the issue, finds the root cause of each and fixes it. Each fix has a regression test, except one configuration-only change. Everything is in one PR. Two items are left, and both need a maintainer: the NuGet credential and the Codecov GitHub App, described [below](#blocked-on-a-maintainer).

All evidence is in [`dev/log/issues/172/pulls/174`](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/blob/issue-172-4d10c904b01e/dev/log/issues/172/pulls/174/README.md):

- full CI logs, run and job metadata, and per-job annotations
- template trees and diffs
- primary sources: lychee's report writer, NuGetGallery's scope attributes, and the CI/CD best-practices document
- the [audit](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/blob/issue-172-4d10c904b01e/dev/log/issues/172/pulls/174/analysis/AUDIT.md) and the [timeline](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/blob/issue-172-4d10c904b01e/dev/log/issues/172/pulls/174/analysis/timeline.md)

## Findings and fixes

### Release pushes and the ruleset

The release jobs (`auto-release`/`manual-release` in `rust.yml`, `release`/`instant-release` in `csharp.yml`) push a version commit to `main`. That new commit carries no checks, so any rule that requires checks rejects it:

- Classic protection with required checks exempts only administrators, and `GITHUB_TOKEN` is not one.
- Making GitHub Actions a ruleset bypass actor is what the hive-mind CI/CD guide suggests. GitHub refuses it for this repository with HTTP 422 "Actor GitHub Actions integration must be part of the ruleset source or owner organization" ([evidence](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/blob/issue-111-9490c2c7fe6e/docs/case-studies/issue-111/data/actions-bypass-422.json); `experiments/issue-111/probe-actions-bypass.sh` reproduces it).

So the ruleset's only bypass actor is deploy keys. A write deploy key was added, and its private key is the `RELEASE_DEPLOY_KEY` secret of a new `release` environment that only `main` can deploy to. The four release jobs run in that environment and check out with `ssh-key`. The C# `publish-current` dispatch on `main` keeps the recovery added by #182 and requires the JavaScript stage, lint, tests and packaging to pass. Their trusted publishing is unaffected: crates.io and NuGet check the OIDC environment claim only when a policy names an environment. `ci-governance.test.mjs` checks the four jobs. If the key is ever missing, both release scripts stop before tagging with a message that says how to restore it, and [troubleshooting](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/blob/issue-111-9490c2c7fe6e/docs/ci-cd/troubleshooting.md#a-release-push-was-declined) has the commands.

Until this PR merges, `main` still runs the old release jobs, which push with `GITHUB_TOKEN`. The Rust auto-release after #182 hit GH013 at its version push. The branch fix uses the deploy key, and a rejected push now names `RELEASE_DEPLOY_KEY` in the recovery message. The first live run of the updated writer requires a merge to `main`. [Failed Rust release job](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/44689293297/job/136147847955)

### JavaScript server and embedded implementation

The owner's review asks for a full JavaScript server/embedded implementation next to the client. `js/server` is `@link-foundation/link-cli-server`: the Rust `clink` in plain JavaScript, with no WebAssembly or native code, for Node.js 20+, Bun and Deno on Linux, macOS and Windows ([README](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/blob/issue-111-9490c2c7fe6e/js/server/README.md)).

- **Command line.** `bin/clink.js` accepts the Rust command-line options. The differential suite checks output, errors, and exit codes for the operations it exercises. It also reads `.lenv` and `.env` first, as the Rust one does.
- **Embedded store.** It writes the same files on disk as Rust (the `doublets` unit store, the names sidecar, the transitions and version-control logs), so either implementation opens the other's stores. The embedded API includes:
  - `NamedTypesDecorator.open` and `QueryProcessor`;
  - the decorators for transactions with crash recovery, version control, persistent transformations (triggers) and permissions, plus triplets over doublets;
  - the advisory `<db>.lock` lock interops with Rust through `flock` or `LockFileEx` on Node.js 26+ and Bun, or `Deno.FsFile.lock` on Deno.
- **File-backed `DoubletsStorage`.** `DoubletsStorage.open` / `openShared` / `openExclusive` port the Rust `DoubletsStorage<usize, FileMappedUnitStore<usize>>` over a JavaScript port of the `doublets` unit store (`unit-store*.js`, `u64` and `u32` addresses). The links are changed in place and written through on every operation, so the file is byte for byte the one Rust writes. `TransactionsDecorator` writes through it directly, as `rust/examples/embedded_store.rs` does. `examples/embedded-store/embedded-store.mjs` produces the same `db.links` as the Rust example on Node.js, Bun and Deno. A `u64` address above `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` fails with `AddressOverflowError` instead of being rounded.
- **Serving.** It has the protocol server (`--serve`), the relay (`--forward`) and the client (`--connect`), over TCP and the JavaScript IPC transports, and the GraphQL endpoint for Deep (`--serve ADDR --graphql`).
- **Parity.** The feature manifest records JavaScript source and test evidence alongside Rust and C#. It records the JavaScript storage limits and the five native IPC kinds (`mq`, `sysvmq`, `mailslot`, `copydata`, `alpc`) that the server omits and the client can reach on supported platforms via its CLI bridge. JavaScript is the third suite that must load all 41 golden fixtures.

`js-server.yml` runs behind the JavaScript stage:
- the unit tests with 100 % line, branch and function coverage on Node.js, then on Bun and Deno;
- the unit tests on Linux, macOS and Windows with Node.js 20, 22 and 26;
- the embedded store example on Node.js, Bun and Deno, whose `db.links` files must be identical;
- the golden unit-store files (`test/fixtures/unit-store-*.links`, written by the Rust `unit_store_trace` driver) and a differential unit-store test that replays random operations through the Rust driver and the JavaScript store and compares every byte;
- the differential tests, which run each invocation through the Rust `clink` and through `bin/clink.js` and compare stdout, stderr, the exit status and every file written;
- the client's conformance scenarios against this package's `clink --serve` (`CLINK_JS`);
- the npm release.

Debug switches: `clink --trace`, `CLINK_IPC_TRACE=1`, `CLINK_DIFFERENTIAL_DEBUG=1`.

**Human action for the first npm release:** add this repository and `js-server.yml` as a trusted publisher of `@link-foundation/link-cli-server` on npmjs.com. The package is absent from the registry, so an npm namespace maintainer must publish the first version before configuring the trusted publisher. The pull request runs a package dry run. The release preflight on `main` prints the setup steps until npm authorization is in [REDACTED] [npm trusted publishing](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers/)

### Fixes found by CI

C# run [43635026592](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/43635026592) crashed its test host with `IpcException: the peer hung up`, thrown from `CloseWrite` on a System V queue. A peer that reads EOF and hangs up removes both queues, its ACK and ABORT included. A retransmitted EOF then fails with `EIDRM` (`ConnectionReset`) instead of reading the ABORT. Rust (`datagram.rs`), C# (`DatagramSession.cs`) and the JS server (`ipc-datagram.js`) now treat that failure while sending the end as a hang-up, as they already did for an ABORT. Regression tests use a link that vanishes on EOF: `a_peer_removing_the_link_before_the_end_is_acknowledged_still_ends_the_stream`, `APeerRemovingTheLinkBeforeTheEndIsAcknowledgedStillEndsTheStream`, and the matching `ipc-datagram.test.mjs` case. Each failed before the fix and passes with it. The JS client already traces and ignores send failures.

The Deno unit tests of `js-server.yml` for 5a7064a5 found that `DoubletsStorage.flush` could keep the old revision. It set the modification time to `new Date()`, which has only milliseconds. Deno 2.9 also truncates the time it is given to whole milliseconds and stores about half of all Dates one millisecond early ([`futimes-millisecond-truncation.mjs`](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/blob/issue-111-9490c2c7fe6e/experiments/issue-111/futimes-millisecond-truncation.mjs)). The flush now asks for the middle of a millisecond later than the current modification time. The regression test 'publishes a later revision even within the millisecond of the last one' fails before the change. The Deno report contains a deterministic reproduction, workaround and proposed fix. [Deno #37212](https://github.com/denoland/deno/issues/37212)

Both findings are root causes 15 and 16 in the [case study](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/blob/issue-111-9490c2c7fe6e/docs/case-studies/issue-111/README.md).

+{"body":"Fixes #199

## Changes

- Wrap local LiNo and binary imports and mutating queries in one transaction in the Rust, C#, and JavaScript CLIs. An import and query in the same invocation share the transaction, including with `--vc`.
- Roll back the batch on a command error. An unchanged LiNo import leaves the journal byte for byte unchanged.
- Checkpoint the store and names once per changed batch. Sync the commit decision before the checkpoint and the applied markers afterward. C# also syncs a single undo image before its first memory-mapped write and drains the async batch checkpoint before closing.

## Reproduce and verify

```bash
work=$(mktemp -d)
for i in {1..10}; do printf '(k%s: a%s b%s)\n' "$i" "$i" "$i"; done > "$work/in.lino"
clink --db "$work/data.links" --transactions --in "$work/in.lino" --trace > "$work/trace" 2>&1
grep -c 'Committed tx' "$work/trace"
```

The original JavaScript CLI produces 100 commits for this input. With the batch, each CLI produces one. The Rust and JavaScript regressions also count four file saves, covering the data and name files at open and at the batch checkpoint. A local Rust run with 100 named rows and `--retention sized:64` also produced one commit and four file saves.

The CLI regressions cover a changed import and a multi-link query sharing one commit, an unchanged re-import, and a malformed query rolling back the preceding import and preserving the version-control head. In the process-kill tests, a FIFO blocks the CLI before its commit. Reopening recovers the original named row and removes all pending rows and names. C# also checks that an export failure rolls back embedded trigger registration and that a successful async invocation has applied every transition when it exits. See the [case study](docs/case-studies/issue-199/README.md).

Local verification passed the 27 focused Rust tests, 97 focused C# tests, the JavaScript server's 100% coverage gate, 15 Rust–JavaScript differential tests, and the repository parity check. The follow-up C# coverage run passed 24 focused tests and exercised all four branch outcomes on the line flagged by Codecov. Rust formatting and Clippy, JavaScript quality and repository tests, and the secrets scan also passed.

All 14 workflows passed on commit `63f8fa3d`, including the Rust and C# matrices on Linux, macOS, and Windows. Codecov reports coverage for every changed coverable line. [PR checks](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/pull/205/checks) · [Coverage report](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/pull/205#issuecomment-7225279659)

The initial PR checks failed the layout test because the generated branch contained a root `.gitkeep`. Its removal is included and the repository layout tests pass locally.

The `pre-commit` executable was unavailable. The applicable checks were run manually. The local .NET 10.0.112 whole-solution formatter reported whitespace findings in unchanged files. Formatting verification passed for every changed C# file. The C# workflow uses SDK 10.0.403.

+# CI/CD Best Practices for AI-Driven Development (languages: en • [zh](CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.zh.md) • [hi](CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.hi.md) • [ru](CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.ru.md))
+
+This document describes CI/CD best practices that significantly improve the quality and reliability of AI-driven development workflows. When properly configured, Hive Mind AI solvers are forced to iterate with CI/CD checks until all tests pass, ensuring code quality meets the highest standards.
+
+## Why CI/CD Matters for AI Development
+
+Hive Mind's AI issue solver is instructed to pay attention to CI/CD checks in each pull request. This creates a powerful feedback loop:
+
+1. **AI creates a solution** - The solver generates code based on issue requirements
+2. **CI/CD validates the solution** - Automated checks verify code quality
+3. **AI iterates until passing** - The solver fixes issues until all checks pass
+4. **Quality is guaranteed** - No code merges without passing all gates
+
+This approach ensures consistent quality regardless of whether the team consists of humans, AIs, or both.
+

+

+> **Tip:** You don't have to pick a template by hand. Run `fix <repository-url> --ci-cd` (see [Automatic CI/CD Remediation](#automatic-cicd-remediation)) and Hive Mind detects the repository's languages and selects the matching templates for you.
+
+## Key CI/CD Principles
+
+> **Pin hosted runner operating systems.** Mutable aliases such as
+> `ubuntu-latest` can switch major OS versions without a repository diff and
+> emit migration notices. Use an explicit supported label such as
+> `ubuntu-24.04`, then upgrade in a dedicated compatibility PR.
+
+### 1. Run Checks Only on Relevant File Changes
+
+**Only trigger checks when relevant files change.** This dramatically reduces CI costs and run times.
+
+Use a `detect-changes` job at the start of your workflow to determine which file categories changed:
+
+```yaml
+jobs:
+  detect-changes:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    outputs:
+      code-changed: ${{ steps.changes.outputs.code }}
+      docs-changed: ${{ steps.changes.outputs.docs }}
+      docker-changed: ${{ steps.changes.outputs.docker }}
+      workflow-changed: ${{ steps.changes.outputs.workflow }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+        with:
+          fetch-depth: 2
+      - name: Detect changes
+        id: changes
+        run: node scripts/detect-code-changes.mjs
+```
+
+Then gate each job on the relevant output:
+
+```yaml
+test-suites:
+  needs: [detect-changes]
+  if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.code-changed == 'true' || needs.detect-changes.outputs.workflow-changed == 'true'
+  # ...
+
+validate-docs:
+  needs: [detect-changes]
+  if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.docs-changed == 'true'
+  # ...
+
+docker-pr-check:
+  needs: [detect-changes]
+  if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.docker-changed == 'true' || needs.detect-changes.outputs.workflow-changed == 'true'
+  # ...
+```
+
+**What to exclude from "code changes" detection:**
+
+- Markdown files (`*.md`) — documentation-only changes don't need changeset files
+- `.changeset/` folder — changeset metadata isn't code
+- `data/` and `experiments/` folders — non-production content
+- `.gitkeep` files — placeholder files with no functional impact
+
+**What always triggers checks when changed:**
+
+- Source code files (`.mjs`, `.ts`, `.py`, `.rs`, `.go`, etc.)
+- `package.json` / dependency manifests
+- CI/CD workflow files (`.github/workflows/*.yml`)
+- `Dockerfile` and related infrastructure files
+
+#### Commit and ready-for-review checks
+
+- **Commit tier (`synchronize`)** runs lint, type checking, and fast unit tests for changed packages, including on draft PRs. Aim for a 5–10 minute critical path.
+- **Ready tier (`ready_for_review`)** runs the heavy unit, integration, and end-to-end suites. Open the PR as a draft and mark it ready when the full check should start.
+
+Omit `opened`, `reopened`, and `edited` from these workflows. To run the heavy tier again after a new commit, switch the PR to draft and mark it ready again, or dispatch the checks explicitly. Keep full release validation on `main` and keep a checks-only manual mode separate from publishing.
+
+```yaml
+on:
+  pull_request:
+    types: [synchronize, ready_for_review]
+  push:
+    branches: [main]
+  workflow_dispatch:
+```
+
+The ready run tests the revision that triggered it. If full verification is required to merge, require a full-tier check for the current revision. A green commit-tier run alone cannot satisfy that requirement. A manual run must target the intended PR revision or merge result.
+
+#### Select monorepo suites from the workspace graph
+
+Have a planner read workspace manifests (for example, each package's `package.json`) and map changed paths to their owning packages.
+
+- Schedule a package's unit suite when the package itself changes.
+- For integration tests, walk dependencies in reverse from each changed package. Test the changed packages and every transitive consumer, visiting each package once even if the graph has cycles.
+- Run every suite when a changed path is unclassified or the planner cannot establish the graph or diff. Explicitly classify shared inputs such as the lockfile, workspace config, and common test setup as affecting all packages.
+
+Emit JSON job matrices, with `[]` for an empty selection, and use the planner outputs to gate and shard jobs. For example, `test-db` can contain `[{ "package": "api", "shard": "1/2" }, { "package": "api", "shard": "2/2" }]`.
+
+```yaml
+test-db:
+  needs: [plan]
+  if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.plan.outputs.test-db != '[]' && (github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.action == 'ready_for_review') }}
+  strategy:
+    matrix:
+      include: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.test-db) }}
+  # ...
+```
+
+### 2. File Size Limits
+
+**Enforce a maximum of 1000-1500 lines per code file.**
+
+This constraint benefits both AI and human developers:
+
+- AI models can read and understand entire files within context windows
+- Humans can navigate and comprehend files without cognitive overload
+- Forces modular, well-organized code architecture
+
+Example enforcement in CI (bash):
+
+```bash
+find src/ -name "*.mjs" -type f | while read -r file; do
+  line_count=$(wc -l < "$file")
+  if [ "$line_count" -gt 1500 ]; then
+    echo "ERROR: $file has $line_count lines (limit: 1500)"
+    echo "::error file=$file::File has $line_count lines (limit: 1500)"
+    exit 1
+  fi
+done
+```
+
+**Synchronize the file-size ESLint rule with the CI check** to catch violations locally before CI:
+
+```js
+// eslint.config.mjs
+{
+  rules: {
+    'max-lines': ['error', { max: 1500 }]
+  }
+}
+```
+
+#### Adopt the limit with a ratchet
+
+For an existing repository, record only tracked files above the limit in a committed JSON object that maps paths to line counts, such as `{ "src/legacy.mjs": 1830 }`. Each entry is a ceiling. Reject a new oversized file and any growth above an existing ceiling. Use `--update` to lower ceilings to the current counts and remove entries for deleted files or files that now meet the limit. Commit the updated baseline with the shrink. When reviewing baseline changes, compare against the target branch so raising a ceiling or adding a new entry cannot bypass the check.
+
+New files follow the regular limit from day one, and existing large files can be split in independent PRs. See the [runnable ratchet example](../examples/ci-cd-pull-request-tiers/README.md).
+
+### 3. Automated Code Formatting
+
+Consistent formatting eliminates style debates and reduces diff noise:
+
+| Language              | Tool                          |
+| --------------------- | ----------------------------- |
+| JavaScript/TypeScript | ESLint + Prettier             |
+| Rust                  | rustfmt                       |
+| Python                | Ruff                          |
+| Go                    | gofmt                         |
+| C#                    | dotnet format                 |
+| Java                  | Spotless (Google Java Format) |
+| C/C++                 | clang-format                  |
+| PHP                   | PHP CS Fixer                  |
+| Swift                 | `swift format`                |
+| Kotlin                | ktlint                        |
+
+All templates include pre-commit hooks that run formatters automatically before each commit.
+
+### 4. Static Analysis & Linting
+
+Catch bugs and enforce patterns before code reaches review:
+
+| Language              | Tools                                               |
+| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
+| JavaScript/TypeScript | ESLint with strict rules                            |
+| Rust                  | Clippy (pedantic + nursery)                         |
+| Python                | Ruff + mypy                                         |
+| Go                    | go vet + staticcheck                                |
+| C#                    | .NET analyzers (warnings as errors)                 |
+| Java                  | SpotBugs (maximum effort)                           |
+| C/C++                 | clang-tidy + cppcheck (warnings as errors)          |
+| PHP                   | PHPStan (max level)                                 |
+| Swift                 | Compiler warnings as errors (`-warnings-as-errors`) |
+| Kotlin                | Detekt                                              |
+
+### 5. Fast-Fail Job Ordering
+
+**Run fast checks before slow checks** to give the fastest possible feedback:
+
+```
+Fast checks (~7-30s each):     Slow checks (~1-10 min each):
+├── test-compilation            ├── test-suites (unit tests)
+├── lint (format + ESLint)      ├── test-execution (integration)
+└── check-file-line-limits      ├── docker-pr-check
+                                └── helm-pr-check
+```
+
+Gate slow checks on fast checks:
+
+```yaml
+test-suites:
+  needs: [test-compilation, lint, check-file-line-limits]
+  if: |
+    always() &&
+    !cancelled() &&
+    !contains(needs.*.result, 'failure') &&
+    needs.test-compilation.result == 'success' &&
+    needs.lint.result == 'success' &&
+    needs.check-file-line-limits.result == 'success'
+```
+
+#### Size jobs and start the longest work first
+
+Aim for roughly 5–30 minutes per substantial runner job. Keep cheap gates fast and shard long suites (for example, `--shard i/n`) based on measured wall-clock times. Set `timeout-minutes` explicitly. Add a workflow test that enforces a ceiling of 30 minutes and a named, numerically capped list of documented exceptions. For a reusable workflow, check the jobs inside the called workflow.
+
+Within a job, schedule independent tasks in descending measured duration with a bounded worker pool. Start the longest tasks first and fill free slots with short tasks. Set the worker count to fit the runner's CPU, memory, and service limits. Keep dependent tasks in order and propagate task failures.
+
+### 6. Changeset-Based Versioning
+
+All templates use a changeset system that:
+
+- **Eliminates merge conflicts** - Each PR creates an independent changeset file
+- **Automates version bumps** - Highest bump type wins when merging
+- **Generates changelogs** - Release notes are compiled automatically
+- **Supports semantic versioning** - patch/minor/major bumps are explicit
+
+| Language              | Tool                                 |
+| --------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
+| JavaScript/TypeScript | @changesets/cli                      |
+| Rust                  | changelog.d + custom scripts         |
+| Python                | Scriv                                |
+| PHP                   | changelog.d + custom scripts         |
+| C/C++                 | changelog.d + custom scripts         |
+| Swift                 | Per-PR changesets + SwiftPM Git tags |
+| Kotlin                | Gradle changesets                    |
+| Go, C#, Java          | Custom changeset workflows           |
+
+**Exempt docs-only PRs from changeset requirements:**
+
+```yaml
+changeset-check:
+  needs: [detect-changes]
+  if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.detect-changes.outputs.any-code-changed == 'true'
+```
+
+Documentation-only changes (updating `.md` files) should not require a version bump.
+
+### 7. Validate the Actual Merge Result
+
+**CI must test what will actually be merged, not a stale PR snapshot.**
+
+When a PR is opened against a base branch that later receives new commits, the GitHub merge preview can become stale. Simulate a fresh merge before running checks:
+
+```yaml
+- name: Simulate fresh merge with base branch (PR only)
+  if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
+  env:
+    BASE_REF: ${{ github.base_ref }}
+  run: |
+    git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
+    git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
+    git fetch origin "$BASE_REF"
+    BEHIND_COUNT=$(git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/$BASE_REF)
+    if [ "$BEHIND_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
+      git merge origin/$BASE_REF --no-edit || \
+        (echo "::error::Merge conflict! PR must be rebased before merging." && exit 1)
+    fi
+```
+
+This ensures lint, file-size, and other checks validate the final merged state.
+
+### 8. Pre-commit Hooks
+
+Local quality gates prevent broken commits from reaching CI:
+
+1. Format check and auto-fix
+2. Lint and static analysis
+3. Type checking (where applicable)
+4. File size validation
+5. Secrets detection
+
+This "shift left" approach catches issues immediately rather than waiting for CI.
+
+### 9. Release Automation
+
+Automated release workflows ensure:
+
+- **No manual version management** - Versions update automatically
+- **OIDC trusted publishing** - No API tokens needed in CI (npm, PyPI, crates.io)
+- **Validated releases only** - All checks must pass before publishing
+- **Dual trigger modes** - Both automatic (on merge) and manual (workflow dispatch)
+- **Commit the version bump directly to the default branch** - The release job pushes its generated version commit (package metadata, lockfile, changelog, consumed changesets) straight to `main` as `github-actions[bot]`, and fails closed if that commit changes anything other than release metadata. Do not route it through an auto-merged release pull request: every release then adds one more pull request and one more branch (a no-deletion ruleset keeps it forever), and a failed run leaves an open release pull request behind for someone to close
+- **A rule-blocked push is fixed in the rule, not in the workflow** - When a repository rule rejects the version push, fail the release with the rule's output and fix the rule (remove it, or add `github-actions` as a bypass actor). The rebase-and-retry path for a lost race is a different recovery for a rejection that prints the same word (see principle 10)
+- **Wait for the registry as long as it really takes, and never republish to find out** - `npm publish` can succeed minutes before `npm view` sees the version. Hive Mind's lag went from 2–9 s to 99–377 s in September 2026, and 2.35.1 took 874 s (issue #2923). A 330 s window turned a good release into a red run with no GitHub release, Docker image or Helm chart. Size the window from measured data with a wide margin (`experiments/npm-publish-lag-2923.mjs` measures it from the Sigstore attestations), log how long each wait took, and treat `E409 Cannot publish over previously staged version` as "already landed", not as a failure
+- **Decide "is there anything to release?" from every artifact, not just the registry** - If the job dies after the publish, the next push sees the version on npm and skips the release for good. Check the GitHub release too and re-run the release without a bump when it is missing; a lookup that fails is "unknown", which never releases
+
+**Prohibit manual version changes** in PRs — all version bumps should be managed by the CI release workflow:
+
+```yaml
+version-check:
+  if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
+  steps:
+    - name: Check for version changes in package.json
+      run: node scripts/check-version.mjs
+```
+
+### 10. Concurrency Control
+
+**Separate cancellable read-only checks from non-cancellable write jobs.** Configure concurrency at the job level when a workflow contains both kinds of work:
+
+```yaml
+jobs:
+  lint:
+    # Include the job identity (and matrix values, when present) so unrelated
+    # checks remain parallel while a newer run replaces only the stale check.
+    concurrency:
+      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-${{ github.event.action == 'synchronize' && github.event.action || github.run_id }}-lint
+      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' }}
+    # ...
+
+  deploy:
+    needs: [lint]
+    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.lint.result == 'success' }}
+    # Every job that writes to main or an external deployment target uses this
+    # repository-wide group, even when the jobs live in different workflows.
+    concurrency:
+      group: main-writer-${{ github.repository }}-main
+      cancel-in-progress: false
+    # ...
+```
+
+- **Read-only jobs:** Cancel superseded commit-tier checks to reduce runner load. Preserve full checks for ready PRs and each `main` revision. Give each job a distinct suffix; include relevant matrix values so different matrix entries can still run in parallel.
+- **Dependent writers:** Use `needs` and require successful prerequisites. A cancelled prerequisite must make its write job not start.
+- **Active writers:** Give every release, deploy, tag, generated-content push, and other write job the same repository-scoped group with `cancel-in-progress: false`. An already started writer finishes while the next writer waits in the queue, including writers from another workflow file.
+- **Workflow scope:** Allow workflow-level cancellation only for events that cannot publish, deploy, or change repository state. An active writer would also be interrupted if its workflow were cancelled.
+
+By default, a concurrency group keeps at most one running and one pending job; a newer pending writer replaces the older pending writer. If every queued write must run, add `queue: max` to the writer's concurrency block (up to 100 jobs can wait). `queue: max` cannot be combined with `cancel-in-progress: true`, and execution order follows when jobs start waiting rather than workflow dispatch order, so write jobs should remain idempotent. See [GitHub's concurrency documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/control-workflow-concurrency) for the current queue limits and semantics.
+
+Use `!cancelled()` instead of `always()` in job conditions so cancellation propagates correctly through the job graph. A bare `always()` can keep downstream work running after cancellation.
+
+**Serialisation orders writers; it does not rebase them.** The concurrency group decides _when_ each writer runs, not _what_ it has checked out. `actions/checkout` checks out `github.sha` — the commit that triggered the run — so the second writer in the queue starts one or more commits behind the branch the instant the first one lands, and its push is rejected:
+
+```
+ ! [rejected]        main -> main (non-fast-forward)
+```
+
+The bullets above without this one convert "two writers collide" into "the second writer reliably fails" — better, because it is deterministic and loud, but still a broken release. `link-foundation/browser-commander` implemented the group to the letter (three language releases in three workflow files, zero overlap in their timings) and two of its three releases still ended on that line. Each run looked like ordinary flaky CI, so the damage accumulated unnoticed: the Rust crate reached 0.10.11 on crates.io while `Cargo.toml` on `main` still said 0.9.0, and the Python package was never published at all, because the job dies at a changelog push that sits before the publish step.
+
+**Do not fix it with `ref: main` on the checkout.** That silences the rejection by building, testing and publishing a tree that is not the tree CI validated, with nothing in the log to say so. The rejection is the honest outcome; what is missing is the recovery.
+
+**Give every write job a push that classifies the rejection, then rebases and retries.** A repository-ruleset rejection (GH006, GH013 — "Changes must be made through a pull request") also prints `[rejected]`, and no number of rebases can ever satisfy a rule; fail with the rule's output instead, so the rule gets fixed (see principle 9). Retrying it burns the queue slot and reports the wrong cause.
+
+```js
+for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= maxAttempts; attempt++) {
+  const result = await run('git', ['push', remote, branch]);
+  if (result.code === 0) return { pushed: true, attempt };
+  // A rule can never be satisfied by a rebase: fail with the rule's output.
+  if (isBlockedByRepositoryRule(result)) throw repositoryRuleError({ branch, version, cause: result });
+  // Auth, network, a missing remote: rebasing would hide the real error.
+  if (!isNonFastForward(result) || attempt === maxAttempts) throw new CommandFailedError('git', ['push', remote, branch], result);
+  await run('git', ['pull', '--rebase', remote, branch]);
+}
+```
+
+- **Never `--force`, and never `--force-with-lease`, on a shared branch.** Both turn a lost race into a silent deletion of whatever the writer ahead of you landed. Rebasing is the point: the later commit has to end up on top of the earlier one.
+- **Recompute after the rebase whatever was derived before it.** A version number, a changelog entry or a tag chosen against the stale tip may already be taken by the writer that won the queue. Re-read the state instead of replaying the plan.
+- **Report success only after the push landed.** A step that sets `version_committed=true` before the push is confirmed leaves the downstream publish job working from a commit that exists only on that runner.
+- **Bound the retries and name the reason in the log.** A handful of attempts with a short delay covers a queue; an unbounded loop against a branch that is genuinely protected turns a fast failure into a long one.
+
+#### Preserve a full check when a commit arrives
+
+Group commit checks by workflow and PR and cancel only superseded `synchronize` runs. Give ready and manual runs a per-run key so GitHub also preserves queued runs. Group pushes by SHA so each main revision keeps its checks.
+
+```yaml
+concurrency:
+  group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.action || 'run' }}-${{ (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' && 'latest') || (github.event_name == 'push' && github.sha) || github.run_id }}
+  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' }}
+```
+
+Apply this grouping to each cancellable job if the workflow uses job-level groups, keeping the job and any matrix identity in its key. Keep the shared non-cancelling group for publishing and deployment jobs. Workflow-level cancellation is safe only when every event eligible for cancellation runs checks without publishing or deploying. See the [language template patches](../examples/ci-cd-pull-request-tiers/README.md).
+
+### 11. Secrets Detection
+
+Prevent accidental credential leaks in CI:
+
+- Include a secrets scan step using tools like `secretlint` or `truffleHog`
+- Fail CI immediately if secrets are detected
+- Never log environment variables or token values
+
+### 12. Documentation Validation
+
+**Validate documentation files in CI just like code:**
+
+- Check file size limits (e.g., max 2500 lines for docs)
+- Verify required sections exist in key documents
+- Check for broken links using tools like `lychee`
+
+```yaml
+validate-docs:
+  needs: [detect-changes]
+  if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.docs-changed == 'true'
+  steps:
+    - run: node tests/docs-validation.mjs
+```
+
+### 13. Container Images: Native Runners per Architecture
+
+**Build each architecture on its own native runner.** GitHub provides free arm64 Linux runners for public repositories (`ubuntu-24.04-arm`). Emulating arm64 with QEMU on an x86 runner is much slower for compiled languages, and building two architectures inside one job makes them sequential instead of parallel.
+
+```yaml
+build-image:
+  strategy:
+    matrix:
+      include:
+        - platform: linux/amd64
+          runner: ubuntu-24.04
+        - platform: linux/arm64
+          runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
+  runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
+  steps:
+    - uses: docker/build-push-action@v7
+      with:
+        platforms: ${{ matrix.platform }}
+        cache-from: type=gha
+        cache-to: type=gha,mode=max
+        outputs: type=image,push-by-digest=true,name-canonical=true,push=true
+
+merge-manifest:
+  needs: [build-image]
+  steps:
+    - run: docker buildx imagetools create -t $IMAGE:$VERSION $DIGESTS
+```
+
+- **No `setup-qemu-action`.** Its presence means an architecture is being emulated; use a native runner instead.
+- **Publish images for every architecture your users run.** A single-architecture image silently excludes Apple Silicon, Graviton, and arm CI runners.
+- **Always cache.** Set `cache-from: type=gha` and `cache-to: type=gha,mode=max` on every build step; otherwise every architecture rebuilds the full dependency tree for every release.
+- **Never gate the release on the image push.** Publish the GitHub Release and language-registry package first, then attach images as they finish. Release notes contain no data derived from image bytes, so a slow or failed registry push must not hide an otherwise completed release.
+- **Assert what you shipped.** Verify that the published manifest lists every intended platform and that each default-branch tag has a corresponding GitHub Release; a missing release is otherwise easy to overlook.
+
+Reference implementations: [`link-foundation/box`](https://github.com/link-foundation/box) and [`link-assistant/hive-mind`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind).
+
+### 14. Lint the Workflows Themselves
+
+**The pipeline is code, and nothing lints it by default.** Workflow files accumulate shell quoting bugs, over-broad `permissions`, unpinned actions and template-injection sinks that no job in the pipeline is looking for, because every job is busy checking the application.
+
+Two complementary tools, in their own workflow, triggered on changes to `.github/`:
+
+- [`actionlint`](https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint) — syntax, expressions, and (crucially) the shell inside every `run:` block.
+- [`zizmor`](https://docs.zizmor.sh/) — security audits: `excessive-permissions`, `unpinned-uses`, `template-injection`, `artipacked`.
+
+```yaml
+- uses: docker://rhysd/actionlint:1.7.12
+  with:
+    args: -color
+```
+
+- **Run actionlint as the Docker image, not a bare binary.** The image bundles `shellcheck` and `pyflakes`. A binary without `shellcheck` on `PATH` silently skips every shell check and exits 0 — so a green local run means nothing. This one detail is the difference between finding fourteen shell bugs and finding none.
+- **Prefer annotations to SARIF** for zizmor unless code scanning is enabled everywhere the workflow runs. SARIF upload fails silently on forks; annotations fail loudly in both.
+- **Set a confidence floor, not a severity floor.** `--min-confidence medium` filters by how sure the tool is, not by how bad the finding is. Review what falls below the floor once and record the decision, rather than discovering later that the floor was hiding a real finding.
+- **Scope suppressions to a file, and write down when they can be removed.** A blanket `ignore` is indistinguishable from no gate at all.
+
+### 15. Audit the Dependency Tree
+
+**Code scanning does not audit your dependencies, and PR-scoped dependency review does not audit the ones you already have.** These two jobs look like coverage together and leave a hole between them: CodeQL analyses your source, while `dependency-review-action` runs only on `pull_request` and only inspects the dependencies a PR _changes_. An advisory published against a package that has been pinned for a year is invisible to both, forever, because no PR touches that line.
+
+```yaml
+- run: npm audit --package-lock-only --audit-level=high
+```
+
+- **Audit the lockfile as committed** (`--package-lock-only`). It reports what a consumer would get, and cannot be turned green by a resolution that only happens on this runner.
+- **Put the job on the schedule**, not only on push. A scheduled run is the only thing that can notice an advisory published after the code stopped changing.
+- **Set the level explicitly.** The default is `low`, which trains everyone to ignore the job; no flag at all is a different failure from a deliberate `--audit-level=high`.
+
+### 16. Prove You Can Publish Before You Build
+
+**A pull request exists to test the code; a push to the default branch exists to produce a release.** Those are different jobs, and a missing credential means different things to each. On a pull request it is a warning — forks have no secrets, and the code can still be tested. On the default branch it is the answer: if any credential needed for any planned release is unusable, nothing the run does afterwards can produce a release, and every minute spent building is waste.
+
+Put a `preflight` job first and make every publishing job `needs:` it.
+
+```yaml
+release-preflight:
+  runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+  permissions:
+    contents: read
+    id-token: wri… it
+  steps:
+    - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+    - env:
+        PREFLIGHT_MODE: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && 'release' || 'report' }}
+      run: node scripts/preflight-credentials.mjs --mode "$PREFLIGHT_MODE"
+
+release:
+  needs: [release-preflight]
+  if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.release-preflight.result == 'success' }}
+```
+
+- **Probe with a write, not with a login.** ghcr.io's token endpoint returns 200 for any scope and verifies nothing — the push then fails 403. docker.io answers an anonymous push-scope request with 200 and a pull-only `access` claim. Open a blob upload session (`POST /v2/<repo>/blobs/uploads/`) and cancel it with `DELETE <Location>`: one round trip, nothing stored, and the only form of the check that is not a guess.
+- **Report every failure, not the first.** The preflight's value is one report naming all missing credentials. A login step that aborts the job hides the rest, so make it `continue-on-error: true` and let the preflight script decide.
+- **Check reachability, not just writability.** A GHCR package is private on first push and stays private until someone clicks; publishing more versions of a package nobody can pull is exactly the compute this job exists to skip. GitHub exposes no API for package visibility (the packages REST API is GET/DELETE/restore only), so this is a manual step that the pipeline can only detect and name.
+- **Prefer trusted publishing.** A credential that expires is a release outage waiting for a calendar date. npm (`id-token: [REDACTED].
+- **Verify the published result anonymously, and separately.** Never gate the release on the push (a failed mirror must not delete a good release), but do check afterwards, with no credentials, that what you published can be pulled. A check that authenticates measures the publisher's view; a reader gets neither the login nor the benefit of the doubt.
+- **Report `unknown`, never a guess.** A registry that times out or answers HTTP 429 has not said the credential is broken, and a run in which nothing could be verified is not a pass. Say which of the two happened: "0 verified, 3 unknown" is actionable, "no failures" is not.
+- **Measure the tarball before you upload it.** npm refused `@link-assistant/hive-mind` 2.40.0 and 2.40.1 with `E413 Payload Too Large` after every build had passed (2.40.1's tarball was 249,862,346 bytes); the largest tarball it is known to have accepted here is 165,142,849 bytes. Gate the actual archive below that (`npm pack --dry-run --json | node scripts/check-npm-tarball-size.mjs --stdin`) and name its largest files. An E413 is deterministic, so fail on the first one instead of retrying. Ship platform-specific binaries as per-platform packages pinned by `optionalDependencies`, as `@openai/codex` does (#4050, `src/native-codex/PACKAGES.md`).
+
+### 17. Tell a Broken Pipeline from a Changed World
+
+**A job that fails for a reason no commit can fix is a false negative, and it trains everyone to ignore red.** Issue #2625 found four of them on `main` at once: a dependency gate that failed every push because a new upstream major had appeared, a cleanup that failed every day because a ruleset forbids deleting branches, a dispatch that GitHub refused before it started, and a log upload that retried a refusal three times. Each one hid the real failures next to it.
+
+```yaml
+on:
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      bump_type:
+        required: true
+        default: patch # the dispatch API answers HTTP 422 without it
+```
+
+- **Gate external state on pull requests; on push, warn.** "A newer version was published" is a fact about the world, not about the commit. Failing the push skips lint, tests and the release for a change that broke nothing; the pull request is where someone can act on it.
+- **A policy refusal is a decision, not a transient error.** `Resource not accessible by integration` (a workflow `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot create gists) and a ruleset's `Repository rule violations found` answer the same way on every attempt. Retry `HTTP 429` and `5xx`; report a refusal once, name what would allow it, and move on.
+- **Every input a workflow is dispatched with by API needs a default.** `gh workflow run` cannot fill a form: a `required: true` input without `default:` makes GitHub answer `HTTP 422: Required input '<name>' not provided`, and the run never exists. Test that each dispatched workflow accepts exactly the inputs its caller passes.
+- **Create what you depend on, or tolerate its absence.** `gh pr edit --add-label` fails with `'<label>' not found` in a repository that never had the label. Create it on first use (`gh label create`) instead of failing a run that already did its work.
+- **Write logs where the upload step looks.** An artifact step that finds nothing warns `No files were found with the provided path` and passes; the run that failed early, the one the artifact exists for, leaves no evidence. Make a missing log fail loudly in the test suite, not silently in production.
+- **Say why a job skipped.** A downstream workflow that skips because its upstream failed is correct, but a green run that silently did nothing reads as "tested". Print the reason as a `::notice::` annotation so it shows on the run summary (issue #2923).
+- **One outcome, one message.** A log that says "recovered and completed successfully" and then "❌ Agent reported error" for the same error sends readers down the wrong path. Compute the verdict first, then log only what is true.
+- **A green bot run can still be stuck.** Dependabot logs `Deferring creation of a new pull request` and exits green while an open group pull request exists, even after a newer major superseded it (dependabot/dependabot-core#16791). Pull request #2285 stayed open 52 days and collected 37 "Dependabot is rebasing this PR" banners while every daily run passed. Check the outcome, not the exit status: the Dependabot Health workflow fails when a bot pull request is older than 14 days or carries more than 2 rebase banners (issue #4055).
+- **Configure only what exists.** A Dependabot `docker-compose` entry for compose files that build every image locally matches no dependency and warns `groups where no dependencies match` on every run. Derive the ecosystem list from the repository and test it (issue #4055).
+- **Group repeated failures by meaning, not by text.** A health check that keys failures by their exact message counts `Could not pull …:2.40.0` and `…:2.40.1` as two faults, so twelve identical failures never reach a threshold of five. Strip versions, ids, hashes and paths before comparing (issue #4055).
+- **Wait for asynchronous release with a bound.** An async database pool closes its connections on a worker thread after `close()` returns. A step that needs "no open handles" right afterwards must poll with backoff and a deadline and name the holder it waited for, instead of failing on the first look (issue #4055).
+- **A reply GitHub cut off is a transient fault, but only a read may repeat it.** When GitHub answers an HTTP error with an empty or truncated body, `gh` prints only `unexpected end of JSON input`, without the status code. Retry that message for reads (`GET`, `gh pr view`, GraphQL queries), never for writes: a write may already have happened (issue #2571). A polling loop must also survive a few failed polls in a row instead of failing the job on the first one (issue #4149).
+- **Take a dispatched run from the dispatch response, not from a listing.** `gh run list --workflow --branch` can stay empty for minutes after the run was created. `POST …/actions/workflows/{workflow}/dispatches` with `return_run_details: true` returns `workflow_run_id` and `html_url`. If the run still cannot be found, warn: the dispatch succeeded, and the job that collects the results reports a run that never started (issue #4149).
+
+## Quality Enforcement Strategy
+
+The templates implement a defense-in-depth approach:
+
+```
+Developer Machine    →    CI/CD Pipeline    →    Release
+├── Pre-commit hooks      ├── detect-changes      ├── All checks pass
+├── Local tests           ├── version-check       ├── Version bump
+└── IDE integration       ├── changeset-check     ├── Changelog update
+                          ├── test-compilation    └── Publish package
+                          ├── lint (format+ESLint)
+                          ├── check-file-line-limits
+                          ├── test-suites
+                          ├── test-execution
+                          ├── validate-docs
+                          └── docker-pr-check
+```
+
+Each layer catches different issues, ensuring no problematic code reaches production.
+
+## Getting Started
+
+1. **Choose a template** from the table above matching your language
+2. **Use it as a GitHub template** to create your new repository
+3. **Configure secrets** if needed for publishing (OIDC preferred)
+4. **Start developing** with the template workflows
+
+The AI solvers will automatically respect and iterate with all configured checks, producing higher quality output than repositories without CI/CD enforcement.
+
+### Add Swift CI to a multi-language repository
+
+1. Copy `swift/ci/` and `.github/workflows/swift-ci.yml` from the same Swift template revision into the corresponding paths in your repository.
+2. Add a caller such as `.github/workflows/swift-checks.yml`. Give it `contents: read` and call `./.github/workflows/swift-ci.yml` with `mode: embedded` and `pipeline-directory: swift/ci`. Adapt the caller's triggers to your default branch and merge queue. [Swift monorepo guide and example caller](https://github.com/link-foundation/swift-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/blob/main/docs/monorepo.md)
+3. Set `package-directory` to the directory containing `Package.swift` (`'.'` for a root manifest). Set `source-paths` to explicit repository-relative paths, one per line, for the manifest, `Package.resolved` if present, sources, tests and shared fixtures.
+4. Keep your existing workflows, Swift-specific checks and release policy. Embedded mode runs read-only CI. Verify that Swift changes run the Linux and macOS checks and that changes confined to other languages skip Swift compilation.
+
+## Automatic CI/CD Remediation
+
+For an existing repository, you don't need to apply these practices by hand. The `fix` command automates the whole flow:
+
+```bash
+fix https://github.com/owner/repo --ci-cd
+```
+
+This command:
+
+1. **Detects the repository's languages** using the GitHub Linguist API (`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/languages`), ordered by the number of bytes per language.
+2. **Selects the matching CI/CD templates** from the table above, sorted so the template for the most-used language comes first.
+3. **Inspects the latest default-branch run of every active workflow** by enumerating the workflow inventory, reading each workflow's time-ordered runs, and validating `head_branch` locally (GitHub's workflow-specific branch index can lag). This catches a failed required workflow on an earlier commit even when a busy workflow fills GitHub's 1,000-result combined-history window or the latest commit has unrelated passing runs, without permanently reporting a deleted workflow's last failure. If an inventory or per-workflow query fails, it falls back to paginated combined branch history; the exact latest-commit query is used only when branch history has no active runs.
+4. **Creates a remediation issue** that lists the failing runs, the detected languages, the recommended templates, and a link back to this document. The issue is created as a **Bug** (with a `bug` label) and its title and text are taken from the [standard remediation template](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/issues/139).
+5. **Hands the issue off to `/solve --development-log --deep-analysis --auto-merge`**, which iterates until the fixes are merged. Every option `fix` does not consume itself (for example `--tool`, `--model`, `--think`) is forwarded to `/solve`.
+
+### Why the issue is a Bug, and what it leaves out
+
+`--development-log` replaces the template's retired case-study-folder instruction and collects artifacts under `./dev/log/issues/{issue-id}/pulls/{pull-id}`. `/fix` never emits the retired paragraph, including with `--no-solve` or partial option sets. `--deep-analysis` supplies the timeline, root-cause, debug-output, and upstream-reporting guidance, so `fix` conditionally omits the matching paragraphs instead of delivering them twice.
+
+That omission is only lossless because `/solve` emits the root-cause wording **only for bug-typed issues** — which is why `fix` creates the issue as a Bug. Issue types are configured per organization and labels per repository, so if the target repository accepts neither, the issue is still created without them.
+
+The retired paragraph cannot be restored by an option combination; `--development-log` is the only supported collection workflow. The remaining conditional omissions are controlled by `--deep-analysis`.
+
+### Language → Template Mapping
+
+The command maps detected languages to templates as follows (JavaScript and TypeScript share a single template, and so do C, C++ and CMake):
+
+| Detected Language(s)  | Template                                                         |
+| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| JavaScript/TypeScript | `link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`     |
+| Rust                  | `link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`   |
+| Python                | `link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template` |
+| Go                    | `link-foundation/go-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`     |
+| C#                    | `link-foundation/csharp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template` |
+| Java                  | `link-foundation/java-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`   |
+| C/C++, CMake          | `link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`    |
+| PHP                   | `link-foundation/php-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`    |
+| Swift                 | `link-foundation/swift-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`  |
+| Kotlin                | `link-foundation/kotlin-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template` |
+
+Languages without a dedicated template (for example Shell or Dockerfile) are listed in the issue for awareness, and the closest matching template is recommended.
+
+Use `--dry-run` to preview the issue without creating it, and `--no-solve` to create the issue without starting `/solve`:
+
+```bash
+fix owner/repo --ci-cd --dry-run
+fix owner/repo --ci-cd --no-solve
+```
+
+The issue is created as soon as the repository has been inspected, but `/solve` starts only after no GitHub Actions run is pending on the default branch, so the AI work never starts from a moving default branch or reasons about runs that are about to change. The wait polls every 30 seconds, gives up after `--ci-wait-timeout <minutes>` (default 60) and is skipped with `--no-wait-for-ci`. While it lasts, the Telegram reply shows a separate "⏳ Waiting for CI/CD" status with the runs still in progress, and when runs finished during the wait their latest results are commented on the issue ([issue #3326](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3326)):
+
+```bash
+fix owner/repo --ci-cd
+fix owner/repo --ci-cd --ci-wait-timeout 30
+fix owner/repo --ci-cd --no-wait-for-ci
+```
+
+## References
+
+- [Code Architecture Principles](https://github.com/link-foundation/code-architecture-principles)
+- [Contributing Guidelines](./CONTRIBUTING.md)
+- [Best Practices](./BEST-PRACTICES.md)
+
+Real GitHub Hello World E2E runs create issues, pull requests and fixture branches. Keep `ENABLE_REAL_GITHUB_E2E` unset by default: schedule and `workflow_run` execution are opt-in through the optional repository variable `ENABLE_REAL_GITHUB_E2E=true`, while manual dispatch remains available. Default unit tests replay captured Agent, Claude and Codex output and verify run-bound evidence. Real runs still require physical fixture cleanup; protected branches keep the run red. Captured regression passes do not establish full #1483 or cross-client delivery acceptance.
+
+Pull requests run essential source, dependency and captured-regression checks by default. Real Docker image builds and container integration in `docker-pr-check` require the optional `ENABLE_DOCKER_PR_BUILDS=true` repository variable; their scripts and assertions remain available. Default-branch Docker publication still builds the actual release images after npm publication. An opt-in PR build is additional coverage, not a replacement for default-branch production qualification.
+
+Pull request events and explicit dispatches on actual feature branches use the `pull-request` source-test profile. It runs the same full default unit suite as the default branch, through the same shared runner, with `--continue-on-failure` so one run lists every failing file. Issue #4025 replaced a 13-file `pr-essential` subset: the other ~690 default tests then ran only after merge, and main went red twice in a week (runs 41801786544 and 42570340658) for regressions the pull requests never executed, while fail-fast showed only the first. The `pr-essential` marker remains as a quick local loop (`node scripts/run-tests.mjs --suite pr-essential`), not a merge gate. No PR-number input or checkout override is introduced. GitHub integration tests and their credential resolution run only in the default-branch `default` lane with `ENABLE_REAL_GITHUB_E2E=true`.

+## Requirements and verification
+
+| Requirement | Cause, change and verification |
+| --- | --- |
+| Investigate every red or incomplete run named in the issue and follow its update | Job conclusions and compressed logs preserve the initial runs, the next two default-branch revisions, and the draft. Narrow diagnostics in the evidence index distinguish checkout policy, process elections, overlapping workflows, registry configuration, runner acquisition and upstream warnings. |
+| Preserve required check coverage and dependency order | The draft placeholder broke `js/test/repositoryLayout.test.mjs`. Remove it, keep the layout test and keep all three required checks unfiltered. JavaScript lint, unit tests, receipts and parity still gate Rust and C#. |
+| Keep each main commit and intentional run observable | Jobs formerly grouped by branch ref could cancel already-running checks and replace pending jobs. Read-only keys now use the push SHA or run ID, with a per-PR synchronize group. Each matrix keeps its identity. Shared release writers use GitHub’s `queue: max` with cancellation disabled. The workflow policy tests enforce the keys and writer configuration. |
+| Fix the actual consensus assertion | Raft can choose a resumed member in a new election. Observe a majority-backed replacement while the original process is stopped, commit through the available quorum and then rejoin the former member. After recovery, require a healthy converged cluster and check the journal and stale-write guarantees. The focused regression rejects discordant and stale status samples. JS Client CI runs the real experiment in both journal modes. Manual dispatch accepts `verbose_consensus`, and `ETCD_TEST_VERBOSE=1` records member observations and etcd debug logs locally. |

The practice crosswalk below records equivalent local coverage and template differences. |

+
+## Template crosswalk
+
+| Practice | Template implementations and link-cli decision |
+| --- | --- |
+| Preserve independent runs | All six templates had branch-scoped cancellation for one or more read-only checks on default-branch pushes. Rust, JS and Python had previously chosen that behavior. C# and C++ already separate writers. link-cli applies the newer guide’s event/revision policy across all sixteen workflow files and enables the existing upstream writer queue pattern. |
+| Run cheap checks first and prove their provenance | Rust and JS contain JavaScript-first examples and policy helpers. link-cli requires a same-commit reusable stage and validates a golden-fixture receipt per language. Workflow policy caps job timeouts at 30 minutes, with named limits for native builds and registry waits. Python, Java and C++ examples assume standalone distributables and toolchains. Their language-specific release steps do not apply to the port and fixture code in this monorepo. |
+| Validate scope and fixtures | The templates use change detection, fresh-merge checks, and size and docs gates. link-cli already uses whole-PR comparisons, fresh-merge simulation, conditional native jobs, strict required status, parity and explicit layout checks. The JS package path filters in this PR now include the shared stage, internal examples and all conformance inputs. |
+| Keep full verification on the current PR revision | The guide offers a ready-for-review trigger paired with a separately required full-tier status. This repository requires JavaScript, Rust and C# pipeline statuses on every PR revision. It runs the applicable native jobs after the shared JavaScript stage and keeps the full check current on each synchronization. The path rules encode the small set of package dependencies and shared CI inputs. |
+| Keep releases independently recoverable | Rust uses crate preflight and ordered Git/registry publication. C# includes NuGet authentication/fallback and package verification. The JS template checks the published package separately. Here the npm tarball gate becomes credential-free, the main writer retains npm provenance and trusted publishing, and a separate job downloads the published version with a clean npm cache and configuration. The client download succeeded locally and the server's exact-version download reproduced HTTP 404. PyPI, Maven and vcpkg release examples target different outputs. |
+| Match runnable targets and runner capacity | The container-image guidance applies when repository workflows build and distribute container images. link-cli releases native binaries and language packages. Its pinned native runners build the platform artifacts directly. Native suites use matrix jobs and keep the dependency order for shared fixtures, compiler output and cross-language tests. |
+| Audit workflow and dependencies | Templates combine CodeQL, Actionlint, zizmor, lockfiles and secret scans, with tool-specific differences. link-cli already lints embedded shell code, keeps namespace pinning rules, scans historical evidence and runs CodeQL, dependency review and package ecosystem audits. Template Actionlint workarounds use a narrow exception or preprocess supported queue syntax. link-cli pairs a narrow diagnostic exception with a local queue policy check. |
+| Recover runner and link infrastructure | Templates use bounded reruns for unacquired runners and recheck intermittent links. link-cli already distinguishes unacquired jobs, protects active writers, and rechecks transient links with archive evidence. A test process cancelled during execution is a different failure and is addressed in the concurrency keys. |
+| Account for external changes and skipped jobs | The repository already reports dependency freshness on main pushes, enforces it on PRs and in scheduled checks, and tracks enforcement failures as issues. Dependabot configuration covers existing package ecosystems. Pipeline status checks report skipped jobs and reject a failed or cancelled prerequisite. Registry diagnostics in this PR distinguish missing setup from an inconclusive lookup. |
+| Keep the repository maintainable | C#, Rust, Python, Java and C++ have hook configurations and language-specific size or static checks. JS adds package size and fast lint scripts. link-cli mirrors CI checks in its hook definitions and uses a lower warning threshold than its hard size limit. |
+
+### Remaining registry action
+
+`https://registry.npmjs.org/@link-foundation%2Flink-cli-server` returned 404 for anonymous metadata, while the client package returned 200. A scope maintainer can validate the tarball with `cd js/server && npm pack --dry-run`, publish the initial public version from a reviewed revision or make the existing package public if it is private, and open the npm package’s **Settings → Trusted publishing**. Select GitHub Actions, set the owner to `link-foundation`, repository to `link-cli`, and workflow filename to `js-server.yml`. Permit direct publication because this workflow uses `npm publish`. Run **JS server CI → Run workflow** on `main` with **Verify npm trusted publishing** enabled, then retry the main workflow. npm currently requires a new configuration to complete a successful trusted publish within two days. Consult npm’s setup and scope documentation for the first-publish or staged approval procedure. [npm trusted publishing](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers/) · [npm scoped packages](https://docs.npmjs.com/creating-and-publishing-scoped-public-packages/) · [npm access](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/commands/npm-access/)
+
+### Provider diagnostics and design alternatives
+
+- **Node FFI and LLVM branch coverage.** Node labels the direct `node:ffi` backend experimental. `cargo-llvm-cov` similarly reports the experimental LLVM branch mode on stable. The real FFI backend and branch coverage remain enabled. Switching to native Node-API bindings or dropping branch coverage would change the packaging or verification contract. The workflows preserve those lifecycle messages. [Node v26 FFI](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v26.x/api/ffi.html) · [cargo-llvm-cov](https://github.com/taiki-e/cargo-llvm-cov)
+- **Codecov and Dependabot.** Codecov’s PGP verification prints the key trust-database advisory alongside a good signature and verified checksum. Dependabot’s managed environment rehashes a bundled CA file and reports that it contains several certificates. The relevant upload and managed jobs completed. [Codecov wrapper](https://github.com/codecov/wrapper) · [OpenSSL rehash](https://docs.openssl.org/3.5/man1/openssl-rehash/)
+- **Codecov GitHub integration.** The coverage comment on PR #208 reported full coverage of modified coverable lines and asked for the Codecov GitHub App. The organization installation list contained no Codecov entry. Installation grants the integration write access to checks, status and pull requests and needs an organization owner’s approval. The existing coverage uploads and coverage checks run independently of that installation. [Codecov report](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/pull/208#issuecomment-7228504998) · [Codecov GitHub App](https://github.com/apps/codecov)
+- **Concurrency tooling.** GitHub job concurrency is sufficient for repository writers. A local action or custom lock service would not protect jobs pending on independent runners. The pinned Actionlint release still treats the documented queue property as unknown. The exception matches that diagnostic only and policy tests enforce its allowed placement and value. [GitHub concurrency](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/control-workflow-concurrency) · [Actionlint #657](https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint/issues/657)
+- **Election observation.** The etcd v3 maintenance endpoint already supplies member, leader and term. Polling it while the original process is stopped provides direct evidence without a new client dependency or an arbitrary election sleep. [etcd maintenance API](https://etcd.io/docs/v3.6/dev-guide/api_reference_v3/#service-maintenance-etcdserveretcdserverpb-rpc-proto)
+- **Windows ring ownership.** The JS descriptor closes before its deletion attempt. The native peer can retain its mapped view while it processes the hangup. Windows denies deletion of an active mapping, and Node 26.13.1 reports that permission error as `EPERM`. Both native implementations close their views before attempting removal, so the JS client returns from teardown on Windows sharing errors and lets that peer remove the file. Fixed-delay retries would keep the JS stream open and still depend on when the peer releases its view. The existing `CLINK_IPC_TRACE=1` toggle records when deletion falls to the peer. [IPC protocol](../../protocol/ipc-transports-v1.md#rendezvous-directory) · [Windows file disposition](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/ntddk/ns-ntddk-_file_disposition_information_ex#remarks) · [Node 26.13.1 removal](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v26.13.1/src/node_file.cc#L1895-L1925)
+- **Windows PID-lock cleanup.** The lock is released by moving its directory and removing the private tombstone. A waiter can still have the directory’s owner file open when the holder tries to move it. Windows documents that an open child handle can prevent a rename. The failed run recorded the leftover entry but omitted its basename and Windows error, so an exact failing operation cannot be recovered from that log. Bounded retries cover transient permission and sharing errors during release and private-directory cleanup. C# owner reads now use the same sharing flags as native Rust and Node. Existing trace flags disclose exhausted cleanup retries. [Windows rename rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/ntifs/ns-ntifs-_file_rename_information#remarks)
